# Draft:Edward (Ted) Zepfel

Edward "Ted" Zepfel is an American former collegiate water polo player who competed for the USC Trojans men's water polo team at the University of Southern California (USC). He was a member of two NCAA championship teams and represented the United States in international competition, including the 2003 Summer Universiade.
Early life and education
Zepfel attended Harvard-Westlake School in Los Angeles, California, where he was a standout water polo player. He served as team captain and earned high school All-American honors.
Collegiate career
University of Southern California
Zepfel played for the USC Trojans men's water polo team from 2002 to 2005 as a two-meter defender.
During his career, USC was consistently ranked among the top collegiate programs and competed in the NCAA tournament.
National championships
Zepfel was a member of two NCAA championship teams:

He scored in the 2005 NCAA championship game as USC defeated Stanford to win the national title.
International career
Zepfel represented the United States in multiple international water polo competitions.
World University Games
He competed for the United States at the 2003 Summer Universiade in Daegu, South Korea, one of the largest international multi-sport events for university athletes.
Water polo has been part of the Universiade program since 1959, and the event features national teams composed of collegiate athletes from around the world.
Youth national team
Earlier in his career, Zepfel was a member of the United States men's youth national water polo system in 2001. As part of national team development squads, he competed in international tournaments across Europe and in Canada, gaining early exposure to international competition.
The U.S. men's youth national team program serves as the primary development pipeline for elite water polo athletes prior to senior national team participation.
Honors and achievements
* 2× NCAA Men's Water Polo Champion (2003, 2005)
* Collegiate All-American (USC)
* Team captain, USC Trojans men's water polo
* High School All-American (Harvard-Westlake School)
* Team captain, Harvard-Westlake water polo
* United States representative – 2003 Summer Universiade
Playing style
Zepfel played as a two-meter defender, a key defensive position responsible for guarding the opposing center and anchoring the defense near the goal.
